tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (agent won't start, no traces, behaves differently in prod, which version is live) rather than internals, explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints...'), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body consistently assumes AWS/Bedrock domain knowledge and jumps straight into check-ids, API calls, and non-obvious edge cases (SCPs, alias→version resolution, OTLP) rather than explaining general concepts like what IAM or VPC endpoints are.
tests.evidence: Simulate the runtime role with `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` for every action it exercises (`bedrock:InvokeModel*`, `s3:GetObject` for sources, `logs:CreateLogStream`/`PutLogEvents`, gateway target actions); any required action `denied` is **LLM-AC-001 (CRITICAL)**.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference data blocks (full API docs, metric tables, error-code lists) are embedded in the body; the comparison table and router table are concise summaries that point to references files rather than reproducing their content.
tests.evidence: How to read each API and metric is in `references/collection-reference.md`. Load it with any row.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked with a markdown link somewhere in the body (router table, procedures, error handling, appendix).
tests.evidence: `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001), `references/api-quirks.md` ... and in Appendix: `references/metrics-and-logs.md` — CloudWatch metric set

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The router table and procedures tie each reference link to a specific triggering condition (e.g., 'Runtime role permission denied', 'No traces from my agent'), clearly indicating when to load each file.
tests.evidence: | Missing VPC endpoint / no private path | `ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints` for bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agent-runtime, S3, logs, monitoring | `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-003) |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at 'references/' with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (read-only API order, permission checks, alias resolution) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible areas like 'When NOT to Use' routing and report assembly leave room for judgment, matching specificity to fragility.
tests.evidence: The permission checks depend on reading the runtime first, so do not skip ahead. If an AgentCore read is denied under the default Agent Space role, that is a disclosed permission gap, not an absent resource.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where the skill designates a primary surface vs legacy surface (AgentCore vs Classic), it clearly marks the default/primary and the fallback, rather than presenting them as equal menu options.
tests.evidence: AgentCore is where new work goes. Bedrock Agents Classic is in maintenance mode... per the AWS product-page End of Support Notice it is 'no longer available to new customers'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach generalizable approaches (resolve alias before concluding production, check role permissions, check gateway targets) that apply to any runtime or agent, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Step 2: Resolve each alias with `ListAgentAliases` / `GetAgentAlias` to the version it serves; treat that version — not the latest prepared DRAFT — as production behaviour (LLM-AGT-007).

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious pitfalls like alias/version confusion, denied AgentCore reads, and no-datapoints-vs-zero.
tests.evidence: "GetAgent shows PREPARED, so that config is what production runs." An agent's live behaviour is its alias → version resolution, not the latest prepared DRAFT.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured review reports and provides a template asset for this purpose.
tests.evidence: `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md` — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report template is kept in assets/ and referenced rather than reproduced inline.
tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced in both the validation checklist and the appendix.
tests.evidence: `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md` — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the condition under which it should be loaded (when a full report is requested).
tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path rooted at assets/ with no absolute path or traversal.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: Both procedures (AgentCore and Bedrock Agents Classic review) are presented as ordered checkbox checklists with '- [ ] Step N:' format, and no detailed sub-sections exist that would need to reference step numbers.
tests.evidence: - [ ] Step 1: Read the runtime with `bedrock-agent:ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` — status, version, endpoint, and the execution role ARN (mask the account segment when quoting it).

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to re-check findings for evidence, correctness, masking, and alias resolution before presenting.
tests.evidence: Before you present an agent/runtime review, re-check your own output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.
